note: Clean pass with disclosures. (1) SOURCES. The administered instrument is the European Portuguese QPPAF, deposited in full by the study's own team (Canario, Abreu-Lima & Cruz, OSF 10.17605/OSF.IO/4K7VP -- reference [28] of the paper) as 'Physical Activity Parenting Practices (European Portuguese).pdf', 31 items numbered 1-31 on the form with the 5-point column headers Nunca / Raramente / As vezes / Quase sempre / Sempre. item_text is that PDF transcribed verbatim, including the four items printed with a full stop rather than a question mark (1, 7, 10, 16) and item 27's parenthetical synonym '(parado/a)', which the deposit's companion translation-procedure PDF documents as a deliberate cognitive-interview fix. (2) INSTRUCTIONS. The form's heading label 'Instrucoes:' was dropped; the sentence after it is verbatim. (3) ENGLISH. item_text_translated is O'Connor et al. (2014, IJBNPA 11:3, CC BY 2.0) Tables 3 and 4 -- the original PPAPP wording for the same items -- reassembled under that table's own shared column stem 'How often do you...', which the Portuguese repeats per item. The 31 Portuguese items correspond one-to-one and in order to O'Connor's items with exactly one omission, 'Push your child in a stroller instead of letting him/her walk?', which the translation-procedure PDF states was discarded when adapting the measure from preschoolers to 5-10 year-olds; that is what makes 32 English items into 31 Portuguese ones. Three items diverge from the English parent and the translated column follows O'Connor rather than the Portuguese: item 9 PT 'futebol ou basquetebol' vs EN 'soccer or baseball'; item 13 PT 'as aulas, treinos, ou jogos das atividades que ele/ela pratica' vs EN 'sport practice or game in which he/she is enrolled'; item 16 PT switches stem to 'Quantas vezes deixou de inscrever' (past tense, 'how many times did you fail to enrol') while EN keeps 'How often do you not register'. instructions_translated and the five option_text_translated labels have no published English counterpart (O'Connor's anchors are never/rarely/sometimes/often/always, and 'Quase sempre' is 'almost always', not 'often'), so those were translated from the Portuguese by IRW -- hence translation_source=mixed and the public_note. (4) STRUCTURE. i1..i31 and IIi1..IIi31 are the same 31 items administered twice (ATP1 and ATP2, ~32 days apart); the wave is already carried by the response table's `wave` column, so both blocks get identical text and a single trivial section_id. (5) RIGHTS. No restriction locatable to quote, so silence is permission. The Portuguese wording sits in an OSF deposit licensed CC-By Attribution 4.0 International (api.osf.io/v2/nodes/4k7vp -> licence 563c1cf88c5e4a3877f9e96a); the English sits in a CC BY 2.0 BMC article ('permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium'). The adaptation PDF records that permission to translate was requested of and granted by Prof. Teresia O'Connor, which is an authorisation to the adapters, not a reservation of rights against redistribution (irw#2121 shape). The instrument is not in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv and no fee, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause was found on any O'Connor/Baylor page. (6) NOT PAPP ITEM BANK. Despite the table name, this is the PPAPP (O'Connor et al. 2014), not Masse et al.'s (2020) PAPP item bank -- the paper cites both and the deposited form is the PPAPP adaptation.

REVERSE-CODING: the ageism block is stored RAW - the burnout block in the same workbook ships explicit '역산' (reverse) twin columns and the ageism block has none, and the negative item-rest values confirm it. STEP 3b: the paper's Methods describes the FSA as '29 questions' and reports alpha=.90 with subscale alphas .86/.79/.79, but the administered form in S2 has 18 ageism questions, the deposit has 18 columns, and none of the paper's Table 2 statistics reproduce (live alpha .82 with the four items reversed; ageism M/SD/min/max/skew = 2.30/0.31/1.389/3.389/0.22 reversing a4,a6,a11 - the best-fitting of the 16 candidate reversals, matching the published min of 1.39 - against a published 2.31/0.46/1.39/4.00/1.422, and no respondent in the deposit has an item mean of 4.00). This is not specific to ageism: the burnout block's published subscale means are each about 0.16 above what the deposited b-columns give, so the paper's analysis file differs from its deposit. The 18 shipped items are the ones the deposit and the questionnaire agree on; the instrument field names the 18-item Korean form rather than the 29-item FSA the Methods cites. LANGUAGE: administered in Korean to Korean clinical nurses (the workbook's own headers are Korean), but neither the article nor either supplement publishes any Korean wording - S2 contains zero Hangul characters - so the study's own English questionnaire goes in the base fields under the translated_substitute fallback, language=Korean, no _translated columns. DEVIATIONS: leading question numbers stripped; PDF line breaks joined; the source's mixed apostrophes kept verbatim (people’s with U+2019, It's/don't/driver's/you're with ASCII). instructions holds the questionnaire's only framing text for this block; section_prompt and correct_response blank by design; a single section_id. The wording is a Korean adaptation of the Fraboni Scale of Ageism (Fraboni, Saltstone & Hughes, 1990, Canadian Journal on Aging 9(1):56-60), published here in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE supplement. instrument_rights_register.csv has no row matching 'ageism', 'Fraboni' or 'FSA'; no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause is locatable for the FSA - the scale has no rights page of its own, and takingageismseriously.org's measures list, which does print a permission statement for the Facts on Aging Quiz, prints none for the FSA. public_note: Item text for park_2024_ageism is the study's own English questionnaire (S2 File): the scale was administered in Korean to Korean clinical nurses and no Korean wording is published in the article or its supplements, so these are not the sentences respondents read. Responses are stored RAW and unreversed, so the four pro-elderly items - a4, a6, a11, a12 - run opposite to the other fourteen (they carry the table's only negative item-rest correlations, -0.15 to -0.23); reverse them before scoring a total.
